title: WorkSpec 2.2 Studio Tutorial
introduction: Learn the WorkSpec 2.2 mental model with one small packing project.

steps.title: 1. Starting State
steps.instructions:
Starting State is what exists initially.

This small world has one workbench, one packer, two parts, no finished kits, and one scheduled task. Nothing in this JSON says that a part is consumed or a kit is produced.

Open the Starting State tab and find parts.properties.quantity.

Changes describe what explicitly happens later. Simulation is the resolved history you can inspect.

meta.title: Pack one starter kit
meta.description: A first WorkSpec project with one explicit change.

steps.initial_changes:
// WorkSpec 2.2 Changes
// Explicit effects for tasks belong here.
steps.initial_generator:
// WorkSpec 2.2 Generator (optional)
// You do not need a Generator for this project.
steps.initial_constraints:
// WorkSpec 2.2 Constraints
// Rules inspect the resolved simulation history.
steps.success_message: You have identified the Starting State.

steps.title: 2. Edit a declarative value
steps.instructions:
Starting State is ordinary declarative JSON. Change the initial quantity of parts from 2 to 3.

This changes what exists at 09:00; it does not describe an event.
steps.success_message: Starting State now begins with three parts.

steps.title: 3. Validate the project
steps.instructions:
Select Validate WorkSpec from the command bar (or press ⌘ Enter).

Open Problems to see errors, warnings, and informational checks. A green result means the Starting State is structurally valid; informational messages are not failures.

Validation identifies the project part involved. Starting State errors must be fixed before Studio runs Changes, Generator, or Constraints.
steps.success_message: The project is ready for an explicit Change.

steps.title: 4. Add an explicit Change
steps.instructions:
Changes are explicit things that happen.

Open the Changes tab and add this handler:

WorkSpec.task("pack_kit").onComplete(() => {
    change("parts", "quantity", -1);
    change("kits", "quantity", 1);
});

The handler is connected to the task by its ID. It runs when that task completes.
steps.initial_changes:
// WorkSpec 2.2 Changes
// Add the pack_kit completion handler below.
steps.success_message: The explicit Change produces one kit and consumes one part.

steps.title: 5. Simulate and move through time
steps.instructions:
Simulation is the resolved observable history.

  1. Open Simulate.
  2. Press Play, or drag the red playhead.
  3. Compare 09:00 with 09:10.

At 09:00 there are three parts and no kits. After pack_kit completes, there are two parts and one kit. You authored the Starting State and Change; Studio resolved what is true later.
steps.success_message: You can now read the simulation through time.

steps.title: 6. Inspect a Constraint
steps.instructions:
Constraints are things that must remain true.

Open the Constraints tab. The rule checks every recorded time and reports evidence if parts become negative.

A Constraint observes the resolved simulation. It does not perform a Change and it does not repair the project.
steps.success_message: The Constraint describes a rule about the result.

steps.title: 7. Follow a runtime violation
steps.instructions:
Deliberately break the rule. In Starting State, change the initial quantity of parts from 3 to 0. The Change will make it -1 at 09:10.

  1. Open Problems.
  2. Find Parts must never become negative.
  3. Click it to jump to its time and affected object.
  4. After inspecting the evidence, restore the initial quantity to 3.

The lesson completes after Studio has observed the violation and the healthy Starting State is restored.
steps.success_message: You inspected a traceable runtime violation and restored the project.

steps.title: 8. Generator is optional
steps.instructions:
You do not need a Generator for ordinary WorkSpec authoring.

Use one only when the world needs computed or simulated behaviour, such as a seeded temperature update. This project is complete with Starting State, Changes, and Constraints.

The model to remember:

  • Starting State — what exists initially
  • Changes — explicit things that happen
  • Constraints — things that must remain true
  • Generator — optional computational behaviour
  • Simulation — the resolved observable history

Projects save these sources as start.workspec.json, changes.workspec.js, constraints.workspec.js, and generator.workspec.js.
